role: The experiment report layer, and the most honestly unfinished corner of the repo: `generate_report` in `html_report.py` is a documented stub whose comment block spells out the full assembly plan, load metrics and predictions from the experiment directory, render six section fragments, pour them into a Jinja2 `base.html` template, write one self-contained HTML file, then raises `NotImplementedError`. Five of the six section renderers (summary, forecast vs actual, QLIKE analysis, statistical tests, diagnostics) are stubs pointing at workspace/plans/html-report.md for their specs.

The one section that actually runs is economic value: `sections/economic_value.py` joins stored per-symbol, per-horizon prediction frames with market data carrying `iv_1m_atm` and `close`, and hands each pair to `realistic_delta_hedged_sharpe`, the Phase 1 analytic straddle engine with tenor-decayed gamma and vanna and volga terms. It renders Sharpe, [[DSR]], 95% CI and cumulative P&L tables plus a cost-band sensitivity table at 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 vol point option spreads, and degrades to a plain placeholder when the IV columns are missing.
reads: A finished experiment directory, stored predictions, metrics and the config snapshot, plus daily market data with `iv_1m_atm` and `close` columns for the economic value section.
feeds: One self-contained `report.html` per experiment once the orchestrator is implemented; today only the economic value fragment can actually be produced.

key_files.purpose: The orchestrator stub: its comment block is the clearest statement of what the finished report will contain and in what order.
The only implemented section: runs the realistic delta-hedged straddle engine per symbol and horizon and renders Sharpe, DSR and cost-band tables.
The planned centerpiece chart, predicted vs realized log-RV with horizon and symbol dropdowns and COVID shading, still a stub.
Stub for the Diebold-Mariano, Model Confidence Set and Mincer-Zarnowitz tables, designed to show a placeholder when the underlying tests raise.
Exports `generate_report`, the package's single public entry point.
